Done. Summary of the work:

**Posted (all with support attached):**

| Entry | Amount | Detail | Support |
|---|---|---|---|
| JE-00304 | $3,425.00 | Dr 6800 / Cr 1510 — March depreciation | DOC-0067 |
| JE-00305 | $1,250.00 | Dr 6200 / Cr 1210 — Figtree license amortization | DOC-0068, DOC-0024 |
| JE-00306 | $20,022.90 | Dr 6000 $18,600 + Dr 6010 $1,422.90 / Cr 2150 — unpaid hourly payroll 3/22–3/31 | DOC-0204 |

**Key checks performed:**
- Confirmed all three items were genuinely unbooked (March activity was nil on 6800, 1210, 2150/2160) before posting — no double-booking.
- Tied post-entry balances back to the schedules: accumulated depreciation $51,375 = 15 × $3,425; prepaid software $11,250 = 9 remaining months × $1,250.
- Verified the FA register's "no additions" assertion against GL 1500 rather than taking it at face value.
- Verified the payroll accrual isn't duplicative: both semi-monthly runs (JE-00263, JE-00299) were expensed and cleared, with the payroll bank account returning to its $40,000 imprest balance.

**Policy handling:** JE-00306 is above the $10,000 senior accountant limit, so `request_approval` was filed immediately after posting (status: pending_approval). I did not split it to stay under the threshold, which DOC-0005 §1 prohibits.

**Checklist:** depreciation and prepaid software marked complete; unpaid payroll left at **in_progress** rather than complete, since the entry is still pending your approval.

One open judgment call flagged for you: I credited the employer payroll taxes ($1,422.90) to 2150 along with the wages so the whole accrual clears against the single 4/3 payroll run. Policy §10 only names 2150 for "unpaid wages," so if you'd rather see the tax portion in 2160 Payroll Taxes Payable, that's a quick reclass.
